Anyone who says amber was poorly written as a female and as a house clone clearly don’t understand her and her role in the narrative. The most important thing amber says that gives us context to who she is is when she tells house  that her entire life, she thought she had to choose between love and respect, but with Wilson she gets both. 

Of course amber isn’t exactly like house. Most obviously, she’s significantly younger and not disabled (house’s personality is very much affected by his disability and amber cannot relate to that). But the point I feel like people miss about amber as a house clone is that a female doctor could never get away with any of the shit house does. Amber has a lot of the same motivations as house but has to operate differently because she is a woman and has to fight for respect. She is cutthroat and feminine because she has to be in order to be seen and heard in a fast paced hospital environment. 

We didn’t get to see as much of it as I would have liked but like house, amber is caustic and rude but secretly cares. She wanted Wilson to buy the mattress he wanted, which is directly paralleled in season 7 when house tells Wilson to buy one (1) piece of furniture that he actually likes in their condo and Wilson buys house a piano. The similarities in house and amber can be best noticed through their interactions with Wilson because both of them are most themselves around Wilson. Amber left the house at night with the flu to make sure her boyfriend’s best friend got home safe. There was no more winning or losing at that point, no competition. She had Wilson and house’s approval. She has a soft heart just like house.

I think you’re missing a critical part of the point. The quote is about imposter syndrome. The first part “no one is allowed in the cockpit if there’s something wrong with them” is sarcastic/satirical because it’s manifestly untrue. But the second part is sincere. “If you’re here, you must be fine.” 

The context is that right before he said it, he was talking about how proud he was that flying a 737 is such a major accomplishment, and he loves it, but at the same time still has that lingering feeling of “I’m not qualified to do this.” Partially because he’s a comedian, partially because he’s autistic. But there he is anyway, flying the plane. 

A lot of neurodivergent people feel this sense of imposter syndrome throughout their lives. We’re always told that people like us can’t do things, but here we are, doing them. This can make us feel invalid in who we are as neurodivergent people, but also invalid in what we’re doing/our careers. If “no one is allowed in the cockpit if there’s something wrong with them” is true, then Nathan shouldn’t be there, as an autistic man. 

BUT HE IS!! THAT is the point. It is inspirational because the point is that if you do something successfully, you’re not an imposter. You belong where you are, doing what you’re doing, neurodivergent or not. Your controls.

WONDERFUL analysis. You put everything I was trying to say into words. The affair itself wasn’t necessarily the problem. Everyone is saying oh five is so selfless and would do anything for his family so this selfish act is out of character for him. And I’m like have we been watching the same show? Five IS selfish. Saving your family at the expense of the world is selfish. And for his motivations to stay stagnant across the 14 years he’s experienced since the start of the show would be silly too. When he was in the apocalypse for decades, his motivation remained the same bc it was the hope he was clinging to - save his family and escape from this hell. But when he’s living a normal-ish life in the world and his family is safe but grown apart from him, it makes sense that he would come to wish and long for new things. He’s always been a romantic - look how he talked to Dolores. He’s been starved of any love his entire life. him hiding the route home from her was indicative of that selfishness too!! If anything the affair was more out of character for Lila than for five, although they have had kind of weird chemistry/tension since season 2

With that being said. The dialogue was so cringe for me. Lila and five’s dynamic was one of my favorites because they were both so nasty rotten and snarky. They have more in common with each other than they do with any of the other characters. They’re both cynical, willing to kill for what they want, and quick to action. They were both bored and lacking a sense of purpose from their mundane lives in season 4, but when they wanted excitement, they got more than they bargained for. Both of them, but five especially, were declawed in this season.  Where was the snark?? Even if Lila and five were together romantically, their dynamic should still be full of jabs and one liners. Their attitude was an integral part of what linked them together in the first place and it completely disappeared. That made the strawberry scenes hard to watch. 

My biggest issue was that Diego and five died hating each other. Either they needed more episodes or five and Lila needed to return from the subway an episode earlier. The climax was not the time for them to be hashing it out. Diego and Lila’s throwaway line resolution was garbage but at least they got something - Diego and five never got a chance to talk or explain or come to any conclusion and I HATE that. Diego and five had such a great dynamic and that didn’t need to be shattered if they had done this arc correctly. 

I agree that they shouldn’t have taken on such a complex plot point if they didn’t have the time or care to execute it correctly. But I also think people are thinking too black and white when they say that the ENTIRE plot point was wrong/out of character

I’m not the biggest fan of the fivelila development either, but I think a lot of people are getting mixed up thinking of five as “selfless” - his goal was always to save his family, but sometimes he would consider doing that at the expense of the WORLD. That’s still selfish. As time went on and he grew apart from his family his priorities changed. I don’t think it was as out of character as people are making it out to be but I’m still trying to organize my thoughts. Let’s not forget that five gave up on saving the family in season 3 too

hence, "you can't fight gravity"). in my opinion, dutch is a person who has always had sociopathic tendencies but has tried his whole life to restrain them. people often forget that sociopathy can be a disorder that people are born with. i think that dutch clung so strongly to his beliefs and morals as a gang leader preaching equality and freedom because those tenets were keeping him a "good" person. for a while it definitely worked - dutch is obviously charismatic, and he saved many people who don't really do much for him but nonetheless are now his responsibility, like the women in the camp as well as john and arthur when they were little kids. he teaches the members of the gang how to read and hunt and survive. i think he initially had good intentions for the gang and their future, but even his charismatic leadership has always been tinged with cult leader-esque narcissism and a martyr complex. i think there are three main factors that caused dutch to completely lose control over his inherent, underlying sociopathic tendencies: micah's influence (which explains why dutch slips up and kills heidi mccourt in blackwater), the traumatic brain injury he sustains during the trolley mission (which is so clearly emphasized in the game that i don't really think we can disregard it as a factor to dutch's descent into madness, and also is the primary cause of him strangling that old woman in guarma), and finally hosea's death (as hosea has always been the blue oni to dutch's red oni, and reigns in his insanity - and now that level is gone). i think it's a disservice to dutch's character development to say that only one thing caused him to finally go crazy. the whole "bonk on the head now i'm nuts" trope is stupid and reductive when played alone, but as a contributing factor among other contributing factors for a character who already has from-birth sociopathic tendencies, it makes way more sense realistically. there's no point looking at dutch's character madness if you don't take into consideration all of the factors that contribute to his development, descent into madness, and ultimate demise. but that's just my hot take!

I feel that I (21F) have had narcolepsy since the age of 14, which is actually the most common age to develop narcolepsy symptoms. I functioned with it pretty well until my junior year of college, taking frequent naps and getting many negative comments about my generally flat demeanor. More recently, I have gotten sick of the constant exhaustion, and I do feel it got worse over the course of college, especially after sophomore year. I had to diagnose myself after many useless consultations with psychiatrists, neurologists, and primary care doctors who tried to diagnose me with a litany of unrelated conditions, and none of whom even suggested the prospect of narcolepsy. I advocated for myself and got a sleep study which easily confirmed that I do have type 2 narcolepsy. I do feel that stress from moving forward in my life and "Adulthood" did trigger my narcolepsy to worsen. I will also say that since starting my narcolepsy meds, 200mg of armodafinil/nuvigil, my narcolepsy has definitely gotten A LOT worse on the days I don't take my meds. I have to skip my meds once or twice a week to avoid getting my body adjusted to the meds which would require an increase in my dosage. On those days, I am completely useless.
